title: The hook chain — how a rule reaches the model
card: Seven machines carrying an injected instruction. The payload is not an object — it is a sentence that becomes a behaviour, which is the case a box-and-arrow diagram cannot draw.
lede: A keystroke becomes an event, a script, a string on stdout, a rule in the model's context, and — if the chain holds — a command that runs. Two of these machines cannot be proven to work, and this page says which two.
handle: The direction guard is installed, correct, and can never fire in this repository: its first line is [ -d .kdbp ] || exit 0, and ruling R8 says this repo never carries .kdbp/. That is a ghost, not a failure — and no two-colour diagram has a way to say it.
source: counts read from the repo at build time: 7 scripts in scripts/hooks/kdbp/, 2 hook events in .claude/settings.json, 14 lines in .claude/register-core.md, 28 skills, 119 classified rules in the enforcement ledger.
